attribution.note: Zitron presents the point as a consensus, but he states it in his own voice and clearly endorses it in his post.

semantics.note: The normalisation keeps the core relationship and correctly leaves out the Goldman-anxiety and 'almost everybody' framing. The claim is firm, not hedged.

contract.note: The investment-payback reading is the ordinary one in context. The contract adds two implicit assumptions, continued spending and a positive required return, and says so openly. That reading is fair and not stretched against the speaker.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous investor analysis (June 2024): the revenue gap to fill grows with each year of capex. That is the cumulative-recovery mechanism. It is one firm's model, not audited data.
Standard time-value-of-money text: at a positive rate, a longer period means a larger future value. Applying it to a payback hurdle is an inference, but a standard one.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's plain reading, with spending continuing and a positive required return, standard finance and the contemporaneous investor analysis both show that delayed returns raise the eventual payoff needed. The relationship holds as a mechanism. No magnitude is claimed and none is assessed.

attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The normalisation keeps the 18-month window and the 'very little new' framing. The 'sort of good' flourish is rhetorical and correctly left out.

contract.note: The plain reading (few substantive new capabilities in roughly January 2023 to July 2024) is ordinary. 'Very little' has no threshold, and whether scientific generative models count changes the result. The contract flags both.

evidence.note: Company disclosure (October 2023) of real use of a vision-assistance app. It is relevant countercontext, but usage alone does not establish how novel the tasks were or how widespread such gains were.
Peer-reviewed AlphaFold 3 paper (May 2024) showing an expanded capability within the period. Whether it counts depends on whether scientific models fall in the intended LLM-centred scope.
SWE-bench v2 (April 2024) shows a low score on real software issues. It shows limits on one task, not novelty across the field.

reviews.rationale: The packet has scattered examples on both sides, but not the representative baseline-to-end comparison the contract requires. AlphaFold 3 and the vision-assistant use cut against the claim. SWE-bench shows limits. None of it settles whether progress exceeded 'very little'.

attribution.note: Zitron's own rebuttal, in his own words. The Murati remark is cited as support, but the denial itself is his.

semantics.note: 'No it doesn't' answers the claim that OpenAI has a secret technology. Read as a present-tense denial of an unreleased breakthrough, it is faithful.

contract.note: Testing his internal state as of July 8, 2024 against public models is a fair, ordinary reading. 'Breakthrough' has no threshold, and technical versus commercial readings could diverge.

evidence.note: Reuters syndication (July 12, 2024) reports the internal Strawberry project and earlier Q* demos on hard math questions. It points against the claim but gives no dated capability measurement for July 8.
OpenAI's own September 2024 disclosure of o1 reasoning gains. Later results do not establish when those gains existed internally.
June 2024 report of Murati saying lab models were not far ahead of public ones. It is an executive statement, not an independent inventory of internal systems.

reviews.rationale: The evidence pulls both ways. Strawberry and the reported Q* demos suggest internal advances, and o1 shipped two months later. Murati's statement suggests no big lead. No record establishes what an internal system could actually do on July 8, 2024, so the contract's conditions are not met either way.

attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The normalisation keeps both parts: the cash burn and 'no clear path'. The Red Queen image is rhetoric. 'No clear path' is partly evaluative.

contract.note: Reading the claim as cash consumption with no demonstrated route to profit is fair. Using Q2 2024 as the window is the evaluator's choice, and is flagged as such. The accounting basis and the industry population are unspecified.

evidence.note: Reported OpenAI run-rate revenue of $3.4B (May 2024), and OpenAI disputed the figures. Revenue growth alone does not show profitability or a clear path to it.
Secondary summary (July 27, 2024) of projected 2024 losses at OpenAI and Anthropic. This fits the claim, but it is an annual estimate of losses, not realized Q2 cash burn.

reviews.rationale: The loss projections fit the cash-burn half of the claim, but the packet has no matched April–June 2024 cash-flow records. It also has no evidence on whether a credible route to profit had been shown by July 8, 2024. Revenue run-rate and annual loss estimates do not meet the contract's measurement requirements.
